title: I Am That: Talks with Sri Nisargadatta Maharaj
author: Sri Nisargadatta Maharaj
edition_analyzed: Revised English translation, most commonly available edition
target_audience: Readers interested in Advaita Vedanta and nondual philosophy
core_themes: The illusory nature of the world (Maya)
primary_purpose: To provide a guide to self-realization through dialogues that challenge the reader’s identification with the body and mind, and to point directly to the awareness that is the true essence of being.

structure_format.organization: A series of transcribed conversations between Sri Nisargadatta Maharaj and visitors, each focused on specific philosophical or spiritual inquiries
features: Recorded in Mumbai during the late 1960s and early 1970s
Minimal narrative or storytelling; focus is on teaching

key_concepts_lessons: You are not the body or the mind; your true nature is pure awareness.
The sense of 'I am' is the doorway to self-realization.
Seekers should inquire deeply into the nature of consciousness and reality.
Desire, fear, and suffering arise from misidentification with the body-mind complex.
Ultimate truth or reality is beyond conceptualization and can be realized directly.
Consistent self-inquiry and spiritual earnestness dissolve ignorance and suffering.
style_tone: Sparse, with little ornamentation—focused on clarity and realization
notable_features: Rooted in the Indian philosophical tradition of Advaita Vedanta
A highly influential text for Western and Eastern spiritual seekers
Emphasis on direct experience over doctrine or scripture
cultural_historical_context: Compiled during a period of increased Western interest in Eastern philosophy and spiritual practice, particularly Advaita Vedanta. Sri Nisargadatta was a humble shopkeeper in Mumbai whose teachings attracted international attention for their rigor and immediacy.
reception_impact: Regarded as a modern spiritual classic in nondual literature
Widely recommended by spiritual teachers, psychologists, and seekers around the world
Credited with reviving and transmitting Advaita teachings to a global audience
Praised for depth, authenticity, and transformative influence; challenging for those unfamiliar with nondual terminology
comparable_titles: Be As You Are: The Teachings of Sri Ramana Maharshi by David Godman
The Heart of Awareness: A Translation of the Ashtavakra Gita by Thomas Byrom
The Wisdom of Insecurity by Alan Watts
